data.name: Prophecy I - The Viking Child
data.detailed_description:
Cartoony side-scroller where you take the role of, as the title states, a viking child, in his quest to free his friends and family, held by the evil god Loki inside the Great Halls of Valhalla.

Fight your way through 16 levels with diverse scenarios, including medieval castles and mountains. Spread throughout the levels are shops in which you can buy potions and other magical items to help you along the way. Before you finally face the Dark Lord Loki, you must also defeat the 8 Apprentices of Darkness.

The game features colorful graphics and 22 different tunes to make the whole trip a bit more pleasant.

reviews.review:
Prophecy I: The Viking Child is a faithful revival of a classic side-scrolling platformer that captures the spirit of early 1990s action games while making it available for a modern audience. Originally developed by Imagitec and published on Steam by Piko Interactive LLC and Bleem!, the game places players in the role of a courageous young Viking whose peaceful homeland is thrown into chaos after the trickster god Loki kidnaps his loved ones and imprisons them in Valhalla. With its Norse mythology theme, colorful presentation, and straightforward heroic quest, the game embraces a timeless fantasy adventure that values exploration, determination, and classic arcade-style gameplay over cinematic storytelling.

The campaign spans sixteen levels that gradually introduce new environments, enemies, and platforming challenges. Players journey through castles, mountains, and other imaginative landscapes inspired by Viking legends, ensuring that each stage offers its own visual identity. Progress depends on careful jumping, enemy encounters, and discovering useful resources hidden throughout the levels. While the overall design follows the traditional formula of classic platformers, the changing scenery and steadily increasing difficulty prevent the adventure from feeling repetitive. Each new area presents fresh obstacles that encourage players to learn enemy patterns and refine their timing as they advance toward Loki's stronghold.

One of the game's more distinctive mechanics is its shop system, which allows players to purchase magical items and restorative potions collected during their journey. This feature adds a welcome layer of strategy beyond simple running and jumping, as deciding when to spend or conserve resources can influence later encounters. Instead of relying solely on reflexes, players are rewarded for thoughtful preparation before tackling difficult sections or boss battles. The adventure also features eight powerful Apprentices of Darkness, each serving as a significant challenge before the final confrontation with Loki. These boss encounters help maintain excitement by testing different combat skills and breaking up the flow of standard platforming segments.

Although the gameplay remains relatively simple by modern standards, its charm comes from its commitment to classic design principles. The controls emphasize precision, while enemy placement and environmental hazards require patience and observation rather than constant action. Veterans of retro platformers will likely appreciate the satisfying level of challenge, though newcomers should expect some trial-and-error moments that were common during the era in which the game was originally released. Rather than holding the player's hand, Prophecy I encourages persistence, rewarding mastery through gradual improvement and familiarity with each level's layout.

The presentation is another highlight. Bright, cartoon-like sprites bring both heroes and monsters to life with personality, while the environments feature vibrant colors that make every location memorable despite the hardware limitations of the original release. The soundtrack includes twenty-two unique musical pieces that complement the game's adventurous tone, giving each stage its own atmosphere and helping sustain the sense of progression throughout the campaign. While the audiovisual design naturally reflects its age, it succeeds in preserving the nostalgic appeal that fans of retro gaming often seek.

Prophecy I: The Viking Child may not introduce groundbreaking mechanics compared to contemporary platformers, but it remains an enjoyable example of the genre's formative years. Its combination of mythological storytelling, varied level design, memorable boss encounters, resource management, and colorful presentation creates an experience that still holds entertainment value decades after its original debut. Some dated controls and unforgiving moments can occasionally interrupt the pacing, yet these characteristics are also part of the game's authentic retro identity. For players who appreciate classic action-platform games and want to revisit a lesser-known Viking-themed adventure, this Steam release offers a worthwhile journey. 

Rating: 5/10
